item.title: Texas Senate Race: Can Paxton Make Talarico's Christianity a Weakness?
item.description: Christianity is front and center as early voting begins in the Texas Senate race between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico. Unfortunately, religion is being treated as another weapon in America’s polarized political fight, not as something independent and powerful enough to slice through our partisan nonsense.
item.dc:creator: Abby McCloskey

item.title: CFPB Should Be a Normal Federal Agency
item.description: Most Americans are ill-equipped to understand the dizzying array of financial products they encounter. Many struggle to contend with payday lenders, credit reports or novel payment apps. A growing share are falling behind on their debt. Meanwhile, a record $16 billion was lost to fraud last year. If only there was a federal agency empowered to protect consumers from predatory financial actors.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Saudi Arabia Needs a New Coalition Against the Houthis
item.description: Saudi Arabia has a serious problem with Houthi insurgents in its large, mountainous and inhospitable neighbor to the south, Yemen. The Saudis have been fighting there in support of the internationally recognized Yemeni government for more than a decade, but the stubborn Houthi rebels — with enormous support from Iran — continue to threaten Yemen’s stability and attack Saudi Arabia directly.
item.dc:creator: James Stavridis

item.title: The War Bump Is a False Victory for S&P 500 Profits
item.description: Earnings season is upon us, and Wall Street expects companies in the S&P 500 Index that aren’t tied to artificial intelligence to rake in profits. That would be good news if it pointed to a broadening out of earnings growth, but instead the gauge is in a Pyrrhic boom created by President Donald Trump’s war with Iran. It’s a bump that we’ll pay for later.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: Markets Are Mispricing Brazil After Lula’s Epic Comeback
item.description: Well, it seems we wrote Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s political epitaph way too early.
item.dc:creator: Juan Pablo Spinetto

item.title: Israel Elections: How to Start on Path to Peace in the West Bank
item.description: On Route 60 in the West Bank, sandwiched between the Palestinian village of Al Lubban Ash Sharqiya and the Jewish settlement of Eli, Muayyad Hussein feels under siege in the roadside kiosk he’s run for some 30 years. First, settlers set the unit on fire. Then they robbed his stock. Then, this month, on Oct. 7 of all days, they hammered a thicket of Israeli flags six-to-ten deep across his shop front and to either side as police looked on.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: Gucci Owner Kering Testing Patience of Shoppers and Shareholders
item.description: Luca de Meo’s honeymoon at Kering SA is over.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Felsted

item.title: Starlink Doubts Have Put a Rocket Under SpaceX and Elon Musk Rivals
item.description: What does a technological kill switch look like? Ask Ukraine. Reports of speed restrictions on its military use of Elon Musk’s satellite network Starlink, essential for fending off Russian aerial assaults, have reminded America’s allies that they rely far too much on access to critical tech that they ultimately don’t control.
item.dc:creator: Lionel Laurent

item.title: UK Budget: Healey Bank Taxes Could Come With Less Regulation
item.description: UK Chancellor John Healey looks set to hike bank taxes in Wednesday’s budget, but industry bosses seem unusually sanguine. Behind the scenes, British lenders are likely assuming the favor will be repaid with lighter regulation as the government scrambles to stimulate growth.
item.dc:creator: Paul J. Davies

item.title: Surfing the AI/Bond Wave in Increments of Fear
item.description: A post-election Iran war escalation could lead to a wipeout on oil prices.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: The US-China Tech Cold War Is Moving Undersea
item.description: When Australia’s Defence Minister Richard Marles described the seabed as a battlefield at a regional defense gathering in Singapore earlier this year, he was preaching to the converted. The security of undersea cables — which carry more than 95% of data flows and trillions of dollars of daily financial transactions — was already top of mind for the senior military brass, geopolitical analysts and government ministers in the room.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Pollard

item.title: Bali’s Tourist Paradise Is Stuck in a Gasoline Queue
item.description: If you’re hoping a trip to Bali might give you a relaxing taste of paradise amid the turmoil of 2026, you might want to think again. Ripples from the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz are lapping Indonesia’s prime tourist destination. Things may get a whole lot worse before they get better.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: A 50% Yield? The AI Trade Is Getting Wild After CoreWeave
item.description: For crazy rich Asians, a selloff in AI-related stocks presents new trading opportunities. Volatility has become their friend.
item.dc:creator: Shuli Ren

item.title: Election Interference Is Hard. Messing With Your Mind Is Easy
item.description: You’ve likely heard the ominous what-if scenarios about election disruptions in November: immigration agents or federal troops roaming polling places, federal officials seizing ballots and voting machines, and President Donald Trump issuing an executive order postponing or cancelling the election. Courts and legal experts have given solid reasons that each one of those potential election disruptions is unlikely. But the threats have served their purpose: People are harboring doubts.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas
